name: Serili
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Taber 1993/1996 SW Maluku survey wordlists named on Glottolog; no grammar/phonology of Serili located

sources.citation: Schapper, Antoinette & Erik Zobel. 2024. Languages of Timor and southern Maluku. In The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia. Oxford: OUP.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Recent handbook overview of the Timor-Babar group; could contain a group-level remark on stress in South Babar languages (second-hand at best).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x, languoid seri1255 'Serili' and its 3 attached references (Taber 1993; Taber (ed.) 1996 Atlas Bahasa Tanah Maluku, pp. 119-121; Campbell et al. 2022 ElCat).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Greenhill, Blust & Gray (eds.), Austronesian Basic Vocabulary Database, language 311 Serili (source Taber 1993), online page.
sources.note: Wordlist with apostrophe stress marks ('lim 'hand', hal'lɛ 'road', to'bɛ 'skin', 'apɛl 'belly'); no notes on stress.

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. in prep./forthcoming. Description of the South Babar languages from 2025 fieldwork (Serili SVE001-SVE011 bundles; a Serili sketch would supersede everything). Currently only the Emplawas Grammar Sketch (ELAR, registered users) exists.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Edwards is the only linguist with first-hand Serili recordings and paradigms; the ELAR handwritten phonetic scans /open in the no-video bundle) carry his heard stress but no prose; a write-up is the likely first statement on Serili stress.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press (langsci 526). Sec. 4.6.5 Babar, pp. 223-236.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Serili. pp. 223-224: Babar languages 'poorly documented'; Serili data from Taber 1993 and van Dijk 2021 (fn. 31: van Dijk's Serili list compiled by native-speaker consultants 1981-83; Edwards confirmed /e o/ vs /ɛ ɔ/ in Serili). Cites Taber's stress-marked Serili forms 'mɔɔ [mɔˈɔ]' (p. 234) and 'oo [oˈo] head' (p. 236). Only general remark p. 118: 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.'

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2025. Serili 1500-item wordlist (bundle SVE008, 15 Aug 2025, speakers Adolf, Michael & Musa Herwawan; typed phonemic file). In: Edwards, Owen. 2023-. Emplawas and languages of the Babar islands. Endangered Languages Archive, collection IPF0417, hdl:2196/28f40694-81ac-4d06-b515-617dd6469394.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bundle description (read online) covers the seven-vowel system and transcription conventions, nothing on stress. 461 phonemic Serili forms, none stress-marked; 10 phonetic notes carry IPA stress: final in [mɔnɛˈɸɔl] 'nest', [tɔkɛlˈbaʔ] 'boil', [abeˈʔa], [bɛʔɛˈra] 'maize', [aˑˈkuul] 'wood', [bɪˈha] 'rope', [lelˈhɔ] 'straight', [lɛˈmɔ] 'when?'; initial in [ˈɔlbu], [ˈlebta]. Primary data, no statement.

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2025. Serili 1500-item wordlist filling in (SVE001), Serili possessive paradigms (SVE010), Serili verbal paradigms (SVE011). Same ELAR collection; bundle landing pages.
sources.note: Nothing. SVE001 description gives only the <e>/<ɛ> convention; SVE010/SVE011 are audio + handwritten PDF scans (SVE010 files restricted). Collection has 26 Serili items, no grammar sketch or phonology write-up for Serili.

sources.citation: Zobel, Erik. 2014 (rev. 2018). The South Babar languages (of Southwest Maluku), with Appendix: Proto South Babar reconstructions. Online working paper, ezlinguistics.blogspot.com.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Historical phonology from Taber's lists (Serili column with Taber's stress marks in the appendix; Serili retains *h, *k > ʔ). Only stress remark is reconstructive: 'In stressed (= penultimate) position, all four vowels remain distinct' (Proto Southwest Maluku). No synchronic Serili statement.

sources.citation: Steinhauer, Hein. 2009. The sounds of Southeast Babar. In Adelaar & Pawley (eds.), Austronesian historical linguistics and culture history: a festschrift for Robert Blust (Pacific Linguistics 601), 91-105. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sister language Southeast Babar only, p. 96: 'Stress does not seem to be phonemic at the word level. Often the same word occurs with different stress in comparable environments.' Serili appears only in the classification discussion (pp. 92-93: one of Taber's ten Babar lists, Masela-Southeast Babar cluster). No Serili data.

sources.citation: Taber, Mark. 1993. Toward a better understanding of the indigenous languages of Southwestern Maluku. Oceanic Linguistics 32(2): 389-441 -- the 193-item Serili (Marsela) list, as keyed with Taber's stress marks in LexiRumah 3.0.0 (Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer eds. 2019; lect seri1255, 191 forms) and in ABVD language 311 (123 forms).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only (article text itself not accessible). My tabulation of Taber's marks in 191 forms: 104 final (lalˈkɛ 'sky', halˈlɛ 'road', biˈha 'rope', taˈʔal 'knife'; mostly stem + suffix -ɛ/-e), 37 penult (ˈbolɛ 'moon', ˈramnɛ 'liver'), 34 monosyllables, 10 antepenult, 5 double-marked compounds, 1 unmarked. No prose statement seen.
